passage: On the terrace above his family's hardware shop in a small town, Chetan had one online post open on his phone: a stranger claiming to have joined a company at triple the usual pay. Phone to his ear, he told Nirmala, the recruiter, "I want three times what you offered." A pause. "That's far beyond what this role pays," Nirmala said politely. "I don't think we can go further. Thank you for your time." The line clicked. Chetan sat among the rolls of wire, stunned. Two weeks passed and no other offer came. He wrote back to ask about the original figure. Nirmala replied that the role was still open, but the number on offer now was lower than before.

qa.q: What was Chetan's demand based on?
qa.a: Chetan based his demand on one online post.

qa.q: How did Chetan feel after the call ended?
qa.a: Chetan was stunned and probably embarrassed, sitting among the rolls of wire.

qa.q: What could Chetan have done instead of relying on the post, and why?
qa.a: Chetan could have checked several sources and asked peers about typical pay for the role, because one unusual case is a poor guide to the market.

qa.q: How might Nirmala have seen Chetan's demand?
qa.a: Nirmala probably saw it as unrealistic and ended the talk politely, and the goodwill was harder to regain afterwards.

grounding: Illustrates demanding a figure far above the market based on one unusual post, so the recruiter ends the discussion and the later ask is at a lower figure.

passage:
Tuan had read a post on a forum the night before: someone claimed a junior data engineer in Melbourne had been offered almost double the usual pay. He screenshotted it.
The next afternoon, on a video call, Wanjiru, the start-up's recruiter, asked about his expectations.
"I'm looking for this," Tuan said, naming a figure far above what the job ad had suggested.
Wanjiru's eyebrows rose. "That's well above the market for this level. Where does that number come from?"
"I've seen it offered elsewhere."
"I see." She was polite, but her voice cooled. "I don't think we're a match on this. Thank you for your time."
The call ended in under ten minutes.
A week later, after two other rejections, Tuan emailed Wanjiru to ask if the role was still open at the advertised range. He felt his cheeks burn as he pressed send.

qa.q: Where did Tuan get the idea for his figure?
qa.a: From a post on a forum claiming a junior data engineer in Melbourne had been offered almost double the usual pay.

qa.q: How did Tuan feel when pressing send on the email to Wanjiru?
qa.a: He felt embarrassed and humbled, cheeks burning, because he now had to ask for less after overreaching.

qa.q: What else could Tuan have done before the call?
qa.a: He could have checked several sources and talked to peers to find a realistic range, then asked slightly above his target with reasons.

qa.q: How does Tuan's demand look from Wanjiru's side?
qa.a: To Wanjiru the number seems unrealistic and based on nothing solid, so she loses confidence and ends the talk politely.

grounding: It shows someone demanding a figure far above the market because of one unusual online post, losing the recruiter's goodwill and later asking again lower.

passage:
The HR office at the private hospital in Siliguri had a calendar of the Kanchenjunga and a fan that wobbled.
Dolma, the HR manager, smiled at Jomon. "We'd like you as our biomedical technician. This is the offer."
Jomon didn't look at the paper. He'd seen a post in a group chat the night before: someone claiming a technician in a big city hospital got triple the normal pay.
"I'm expecting this," he said, and named a figure far higher.
Dolma's smile faded a little. "That's what we pay senior engineers with ten years' experience. Where have you seen it for this level?"
"Online."
"I'm sorry, Jomon. We can't go anywhere near that. I think we should stop here."
Two weeks later, with no other offer, Jomon came back to the same office. "Is the post still available? At the first figure is fine." Dolma was polite, but she said she'd need to check again.

qa.q: What did Dolma say the figure Jomon named was normally paid for?
qa.a: She said it is what they pay senior engineers with ten years' experience.

qa.q: Why didn't Jomon look at the offer paper, and what does that suggest about his feelings?
qa.a: He was so set on the number from the group chat that he felt overconfident and sure he deserved more, so he didn't even read what was offered.

qa.q: What would you change first in Jomon's approach?
qa.a: Check the offer and compare it with several realistic sources, then ask for a slightly higher figure with reasons, instead of relying on one post.

qa.q: How is Dolma affected by Jomon's demand?
qa.a: Dolma loses some goodwill toward him, so even when he returns and accepts the first figure, she is cautious and needs to check again.

grounding: It shows someone demanding a figure far above the market because of one unusual online post, ending the discussion and later having to ask at a lower figure.
